checks: Verified that the sole decoded field change is an appended proof sentence identifying the three actual integer fibers as the domain of the mixed maximum. This matches the revised three-fiber theorem, while the ordinary projected law continues to maximize over all continuous points via its supporting and separating caps and its compact support.

Verified both source digests and locators. In 1d1be0b22c707856 §5 the comparison follows (10); in 7ff8cebaefda7361 §§1–5 supplies the ordinary cap argument and §6 (15)–(18) applies to this E_ε with N=2. The frozen proof proves the moving-law calculation directly.

All vertices of E_ε belong to T because each nonzero vertex has nonnegative coordinates with sum h+ε<1. The map εI+g1ᵀ acts by ε on the coordinate-sum-zero subspace and by ε+h on g, so the volume ratio is ε^(d−1)(ε+h), positive, strictly increasing and tending to zero for d≥2. Independently tested the exact integer-scaled determinant for 60 matrices with d=2,…,16 and four rational ε in the allowed range.

The barycentric coupling is uniform on E_ε because it is the affine image of uniform simplex barycentrics by an invertible map. R=1 occurs on a null facet. For any moving center tending to g and unit normal tending to the i-th canonical normal, the limiting signed margin is strictly positive for i=0 and strictly negative for i≥1 almost surely. Dominated convergence yields probabilities 1 and 0 respectively, with average 1/(d+1).

Both parts of the projected measure are absolutely continuous. Through-point unit-normal cap masses are jointly continuous, the compact sphere yields a continuous minimum, and supporting or separating caps have zero mass off int T. Thus the maximum is attained. At any maximizer the g comparison and each homothetic cap give (1−λ_i)^d≥Γ_d−a/(2V). The root is smooth at Γ_d>0 and the coordinate-sum identity bounds deviations on both sides by O(a), uniformly over maximizers.

The canonical upper estimates have continuous-body term −2κ(λ_i−1/m) and added term a c_i+o(a). Averaging cancels the zero-sum displacement. The prescribed lower-bound point has positive coordinates summing to one for small a and exactly equalizes all first-order canonical costs.

For a violating sequence of arbitrary normals through the prescribed point, sphere compactness, cap continuity and nonnegative added mass imply that the limiting T cap has volume at most Γ_dV. The frozen profile identifies an exact canonical equality direction. Near that direction the vertex margins have one positive and d negative signs, so the cap simplex has the stated product of d edge fractions. The denominators stay strictly positive. The derivative in y is continuous there and equals −κ times the barycentric linear part at the canonical pair. Integration along the O(a) center displacement leaves o(a) for any rate of angular convergence. The unperturbed term F(g,u_ε) is kept at its exact lower bound Γ_dV, which suffices for the contradiction after adding a c_i+o(a).

Subtracting Γ_d after normalizing the raw expansion gives [a(1/m−Γ_d)+o(a)]/(2V+a). Two canonical caps have simultaneous strict inequalities on an open positive-volume subset: set the first two barycentric coordinates to 5/(4m) and the remaining coordinates equally positive. Thus mΓ_d>1 for d≥2. The exact triple census gives projected mass 2V+a and mixed maximum Γ_dV+a, and strict monotonicity of a(ε) permits the stated right derivatives in a.

overlap.comparison: This fact uses canonical cap equalization and the same near-critical direction argument for a fixed exterior facet-roof strip, with one copy of uniform simplex volume and a limiting law on the fixed facet. The present interior thin simplex converges to a segment from vertex to centroid, with a different allowed perturbation and no conclusion from the fixed-roof hypotheses.

The simplex centroid equality directions and uniform simplex maximum agree with the unperturbed inputs. The accepted result concerns normalized uniform convex-body laws, while the projected law here has an interior density increment.
